correctness.rationale: Invertibility of the weighted permutation square matrix forces disjoint support columns for any algebra isomorphism and hence a monomial matrix; any compatible permutation is a directed-cycle rotation. Diagonal scaling changes P=prod a_i^(2^(n-1-i)) by an (2^n-1)-st power and one rotation squares its class. Thus isomorphism classes are squaring orbits in G=F_q^*/(F_q^*)^(2^n-1), class count sum_{d|g} phi(d)/ord_d(2), automorphism size g*n/ord_d(2), and idempotents 1+g iff class trivial, else 1. Uniform final weight makes the class uniform. Reconstructed independent finite-field brute-force orbit, rational automorphism, and idempotent tests, including n=1, q=3,5,7. Proof covers arbitrary finite prime powers without extrapolating experiments.
